html:
The Nepalese Civil War was a ten-year revolt by Maoist communists against the government of Nepal, from 1996 to 2006. About 17,000 people died. It ended with the fall of the monarchy.

Nepal had won a parliament in 1990, but the hill villages stayed poor and governments rose and fell every year. On 13 February 1996 a small Maoist party led by a former teacher known as Prachanda attacked police posts in the western hills. It promised land, an end to caste and to the king's rule, and rights for women and ethnic groups. Many of its fighters were young women. Within a few years it ran much of the countryside.

In June 2001 the crown prince shot dead the king, the queen and seven other members of the royal family at a dinner, and then himself. The king's brother Gyanendra took the throne. He sent the army against the rebels and in 2005 dismissed the government and took power himself.

That drove the political parties and the Maoists together. Nineteen days of street protests in April 2006 forced the king to recall parliament, and a peace agreement was signed on 21 November.

In 2008 an elected assembly, with the Maoists as the largest party, ended the 240-year-old monarchy. Nepal became a federal republic.
sum: The Nepalese Civil War was a ten-year revolt by Maoist communists against the government of Nepal, from 1996 to 2006. About 17,000 people died. It ended with the fall of the monarchy.
